items.problem: Row-based list surfaces have no measure. The token system defines only --measure (38rem) for prose and --shell (76rem) for the page shell, with nothing in between, so every list row stretches to the full 1216px shell and its metadata is pushed to the far right edge. On /tools the jump list sets the word 'agents' at x=145 and its count '2' at x=1280 - 1135px of empty space bridged only by a hairline. On /wiki the entry name sits at the left edge and its type plus status badge at the right, up to 1100px away, for 95 consecutive rows. On /data eleven rows separate a title from its file path across roughly 700px. The reader must traverse the full viewport width to bind a name to the one fact that qualifies it, on the site's primary navigation surfaces. The 390px capture proves the association is achievable: at that width the type label moves directly under the name and left-aligns, so the mobile treatment reads better than the desktop one.
items.invariant: On any row-based list surface, the horizontal gap between a row's primary label and its right-most metadata cell is at most 24rem; equivalently, list rows are constrained to a list measure token rather than defaulting to --shell.
items.prescription: Add a third width token (e.g. --measure-list: 46rem) between --measure and --shell and apply it to the /tools category jump list, the /wiki index rows and the /data resource rows; or keep full width and move the metadata to a fixed column immediately after the longest label rather than right-aligning it to the container edge. Checked R1-R6: none governs measure, so no rule constrains this remedy.

items.problem: Section rules are scoped to the shell while the content they divide is scoped to --measure, so a 1152px rule repeatedly underlines a 605px column and points at empty space. Worst on the wiki entry - the site's most numerous template at 495 records - where the body runs 2400px down a 610px left-hand column while the header rule, the FACTS block and the footer columns all span the full 1152px: the page has two conflicting widths and the eye must re-anchor at every transition. The same defect appears on the article (605px prose under a 1152px rule), the colophon (600px prose, 1152px rule over a 480px definition list) and /data. Three different left edges appear on one wiki entry page - prose at 97, FACTS values at 205, APPEARS IN at 497 - none sharing a grid line.
items.invariant: Every horizontal rule spans exactly the width of the content block it divides, and every column start on a page aligns to a shared grid track.
items.prescription: Scope section rules to the same width container as the content beneath them rather than to .shell. On the wiki entry, either widen the prose block toward the shell or narrow the header rule, FACTS block and cross-reference columns to the prose measure so the template resolves to one width. Checked R1-R6: none governs rule width.

items.problem: Separation is carried by borders rather than by rhythm, and the default state is boxed. Every row on every list surface carries a hairline rule: 24 on the home feed, 95 on /wiki, 396 on /catalog, 12 on the /tools jump list, 14 on /data. The catalog table is additionally wrapped in a full outer box border, making it read as a card. On top of that, a bordered status pill is drawn on every single row including ACTIVE, which is roughly 70% of /wiki and nearly all of /catalog - 396 plus 95 boxes spent marking the unexceptional case, which leaves the exceptional case (DEPRECATED, RETIRED, DEAD) no more visually prominent than the norm. The wiki entry header adds five bordered pills in a row in two colour families.
items.invariant: A list surface draws a rule only at a group boundary, not between every pair of sibling rows; and a status marker is rendered as a bordered box only for non-default states.
items.prescription: Drop the per-row hairline on /wiki, /tools and /data and let uniform row height plus a consistent left edge carry the separation, keeping a rule only where a category changes. Drop the catalog's outer table border. Render ACTIVE as plain muted small-caps text with no border and reserve the boxed ember treatment for DEPRECATED, RETIRED and DEAD only. Checked R1: removing borders must not push any text below the contrast floor, so ACTIVE must stay at --muted or darker, never lighter.

items.problem: The accent is applied to every link, and on a reference site nearly every noun is a link, so colour has stopped marking state and become the body colour. /catalog renders 396 indigo model names beside 396 indigo dates - two fully coloured columns; /blog is 100% indigo content; the /learn descriptions are speckled with indigo mid-sentence. The stylesheet's own comment states the intent - indigo means 'follow this' - which the render contradicts at this density, and it neutralises ember as an alarm because a red badge no longer stands out against an already coloured field. Compounding it, one semantic gets three treatments: a link to a record is dark serif on the /wiki index, indigo bold serif on the /blog index and indigo mono on /catalog. On /data one link is blue and underlined while eleven sibling links in the same rows carry no link treatment at all, so what is clickable is unreadable.
items.invariant: Within any single list or table surface, at most one column carries the accent colour; and one semantic - a link to a record - has exactly one visual treatment across every template.
items.prescription: Set list and table links in --ink and carry affordance with an underline (or underline-on-hover) rather than with hue, reserving --accent for prose inline links and for the one primary action per surface; then apply that single treatment to the /wiki, /blog and /catalog indexes alike, and give the /data right-hand paths the same treatment as the /dataset link above them. Checked R1: any link-colour change must keep axe contrast clean in both themes; checked R5: if affordance moves to an underline, the focus indicator must stay visually distinct from it.

items.problem: At 390px the catalog - a price table, the reason a reader comes to this page - shows only the MODEL column. The six data columns (provider, in/Mtok, out/Mtok, context, status, read) are correctly moved into an in-container horizontal scroller per R2, but the static render shows no cue that they exist: no edge fade, no shadow, no scroll hint, no visible scrollbar track. A reader on a phone sees a bordered box listing 396 model names and no prices, with nothing indicating the prices are one sideways swipe away.
items.invariant: Where a table scrolls inside its own container, the container renders a persistent visual indication of the off-screen content that is present in a static render, not only on interaction.
items.prescription: Keep the in-container scroll that R2 requires and add a persistent right-edge gradient mask on the scroller plus a sticky MODEL column so the identifier stays visible while the numeric columns move. Do not resolve this by letting the page scroll horizontally - R2 forbids it.

items.problem: The blog index is the site's least dense and least controlled surface. Its four post titles are set across the full 1150px shell at roughly 110 characters per line while the intro paragraph directly above them is correctly held to about 62 characters, so the same page shows a controlled measure and an uncontrolled one within 40px of each other; two of the four titles wrap awkwardly as a result. The list occupies 200px of a 900px viewport and the footer sits at y=620, leaving roughly 300px of empty page below it at 1440. The template gives a reader four rows on a screen that comfortably holds far more information per row.
items.invariant: No headline or title in a list row exceeds 75 characters per line at 1440px.
items.prescription: Constrain the blog index title column to the list measure introduced in I1 and use the freed right-hand space for per-post metadata (kind, and the standfirst if one exists in the data) so the row carries more than a date and a title. Note: introducing text not already present in the data would be out of scope under charter slot 1 - use only fields already rendered elsewhere.

items.problem: The focus-indicator sweep on /catalog reports PASS while having examined 150 of 817 focusable elements: 'STOPPED AT THE 150-STOP CAP, the rest unswept'. 667 elements - the overwhelming majority of the catalog's tab stops, and every stop below roughly the fiftieth table row - have never been checked for a focus indicator, and the check reports success anyway. This is the exact failure mode R5's own preserved post-mortem was written about: a traversal that quits early passes for the wrong reason and keeps passing for as long as it exists. R5 requires focus visibility 'on the whole page', and this run does not establish it for /catalog.
items.evidence: verify-design.mjs run output, 2026-08-31: 'PASS every tab stop shows a focus indicator /catalog - 150 of 817 focusable element(s) - STOPPED AT THE 150-STOP CAP, the rest unswept'
items.invariant: A focus traversal that does not visit every focusable element on the page reports FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS.
items.prescription: Change the cap behaviour so an incomplete sweep is not a pass: either raise the cap above the page's actual focusable count, or sample deterministically across the whole tab order (first 50, last 50, and an even stride through the middle) and report the sampling explicitly. Do not change the artifact for this item.

items.target: evidence rig - scripts/verify-design.mjs axe route set
items.problem: axe-core runs on four routes (/, /wiki/concept/ai-winter, /catalog, /tools) while the screenshot rig samples ten distinct templates. Six templates have never been axe-tested in either theme: the blog index, the article, the wiki index, /learn, /colophon and /data. The charter's oracle table describes this source as 'axe-core, both themes, every sampled route', which the current route set does not satisfy, so the accessibility score rests on 40% of the templates the loop otherwise judges. The blog index in particular is the surface most changed by I4 and I6 and is not covered.
items.evidence: verify-design.mjs run output, 2026-08-31 (axe section lists 4 routes); loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/manifest.json (10 labels)
items.invariant: The axe route set is identical to the set of route labels in the screenshot manifest.
items.prescription: Extend the axe route list in scripts/verify-design.mjs to the ten routes in manifest.json so R1's 'every sampled route' is literally true. Expect this to surface new violations; those become artifact items in a later iteration, not this one.

items.problem: Home feed rows have ragged heights because the trailing 'source' link wraps to a second line on some rows and not others, with no pattern a reader can predict: rows 6, 7, 8, 9, 14, 15 and 16 are two lines while their neighbours are one. The result is a column of rules at irregular intervals down the page, which destroys the vertical rhythm that lets a reader scan 24 dated changes quickly. The same wrap appears on the wiki entry FACTS block, where two of four rows wrap and two do not.
items.invariant: Within one list surface, every row that carries the same fields renders at the same height.
items.prescription: Give the trailing source link a fixed right-hand column of its own so it never participates in the wrap of the change description, or set the description to a measure that leaves guaranteed room for it on one line. Related to I1 - a list measure token would make this column allocation natural.

items.problem: The catalog filter row mixes two radii vocabularies and two control idioms side by side: the NAME CONTAINS text input and the Clear button use the site's square-cornered thin-border treatment, while the PROVIDER and STATUS controls are unstyled native selects with a noticeably larger corner radius and a platform chevron. Placed within 150px of each other in the same row, they read as two different design systems, and the native chrome is the one element on the site that looks inherited rather than chosen.
items.invariant: Every interactive control on a surface shares one border-radius value and one border treatment from the token system.
items.prescription: Style the selects to the same radius, border and type as the text input, keeping a native select element so R4's keyboard reachability and activation still hold; do not replace them with a custom listbox widget, which would put R4 at risk for no visual gain.

items.problem: The top changed-feed row is followed by a 12-line indented WHAT IT MEANS explainer that occupies roughly 130px of the 900px first screen, so one change out of 24 consumes more vertical space above the fold than the next eight combined. Whether that is correct depends on whether a reader arriving at the home page wants the single most consequential change explained or wants the widest possible scan of what moved - a question no screenshot answers, and one that cannot be settled by changing presentation without also deciding an editorial priority.
items.prescription: Keeper decision, not a loop change. If the explainer should stay prominent, the current treatment is right and this item closes. If scan breadth wins, the presentational move is to collapse the explainer behind a disclosure - but that changes what the first screen says, and R6 exists precisely to stop the loop from quietly relocating the site's substance.

items.target: app/ home page template (EVERYTHING HERE block)
items.problem: The EVERYTHING HERE block draws two nearly parallel full-width rules 13px apart - one under the section label and one above the first row of cells - so the eye reads a doubled divider where one is intended. The second-row cells (Tutorials, Blog, Impossible to Routine) carry no rule above them, so the divider logic is applied to the first row only and the grid reads as inconsistently ruled.
items.invariant: No two horizontal rules of the same weight appear within 2rem of each other spanning the same width.
items.prescription: Remove the per-cell top rules in the first row and keep only the section rule under the EVERYTHING HERE label; or remove the section rule and keep the per-cell rules on every row rather than the first. Either resolves the doubling and the row inconsistency together.

items.problem: In the EVERYTHING HERE block, the Tools cell alone carries a 2px indigo underline under its description line that no sibling cell has, and it appears at identical coordinates in both the light and dark captures. I cannot determine from the evidence whether this is a real style anomaly or a hover state rendered because the capture leaves the pointer parked over that cell - the oracle table declares screenshots blind to hover states, so this is undecidable from the evidence I have, and filing it as an artifact defect would risk sending an implementer after a style that does not exist.
items.invariant: Captures render no hover state: the pointer is moved outside the viewport before every screenshot.
items.prescription: In tools/ui-evidence.mjs, move the pointer to an off-canvas coordinate immediately before each capture (and consider emulating a no-hover pointer plus prefers-reduced-motion), so the next iteration's home captures disambiguate this. If the underline persists after that change, re-file it as a ui-fixable coherence item.
